My research explores connections between quantum gravity, holography, geometry, gauge theory, and mathematical physics.

## Spectral Holography

**MSci Research Project, University of Nottingham**

*Emergent Geometry, Gauge Theory, and Gravity from Modular Graph Entanglement*

**Supervisor:** Prof. Anastasios Avgoustidis  
**Coauthor:** Rhys Hender

**Overview**

A spectral framework connecting weighted graphs, operator algebras, modular structure, gauge holonomies, and emergent geometry. The project develops explicit constructions linking spectral data to geometric and gauge-theoretic structures, while separating proved results from conjectural physical interpretations.

<details>
<summary><strong>Motivation</strong></summary>

The project asks whether geometric and gravitational structure can be reconstructed from algebraic and spectral data rather than assumed from the outset. It combines operator algebras, modular flow, graph spectra, gauge holonomies, and geometric invariants into a single framework, with careful separation between mathematical results and conjectural physics.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Topics studied</strong></summary>

- Von Neumann algebras, crossed products, modular theory, and modular flow
- Spectral graph theory, weighted Laplacians, and spectral embeddings
- Gauge theory, Lie algebras, holonomies, and twisted Laplacians
- Differential geometry, curvature, and emergent metric structure
- Holography, entanglement, and quantum gravitational interpretations
- Topological sectors, representation theory, and collective modes

</details>

## Clock Geometry in AdS3 Gravity

*The York Hamiltonian as a Curvature-Generating Function*

**Independent research · single author**

**Overview**

Three-dimensional AdS gravity has a completely known classical solution space on a closed surface of genus $g\geq2$, together with a canonical constant-mean-curvature foliation. The paper shows that the resulting family of York-time Hamiltonians is not independent: an exact scaling identity collapses it onto a single universal profile.

The profile connects the Weil–Petersson geometry of the small-momentum regime to Hubbard–Masur extremal length at large momentum, while the holographic interpretation gives a semiclassical stress-tensor dilation law and a prediction for the sextic boundary effective-action term.

<details>
<summary><strong>Motivation</strong></summary>

The problem of time asks how physical evolution can be defined when the Hamiltonian of a generally covariant theory is itself a constraint. AdS$_3$ provides an unusually rigid setting in which different clock choices can be studied explicitly. York time supplies a geometrically distinguished CMC clock, allowing the resulting Hamiltonians to be compared exactly rather than only perturbatively.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Topics studied</strong></summary>

- Teichmüller theory and Weil–Petersson geometry
- AdS$_3$ geometry, the Mess parametrisation, and CMC foliations
- Hamiltonian reduction of 2+1 gravity and York slicing
- Elliptic PDE, maximum principles, and variational methods
- Symplectic geometry, polarisation, clocks, and the problem of time
- Quadratic differentials, measured foliations, and extremal length
- Holographic renormalisation, Brown–York stress tensors, and Virasoro geometry
- Virasoro TQFT and $T\bar{T}$ deformations

</details>

[Project PDF →](york_time%20%281%29.pdf)

## Hodge-Relative Completions of Characteristic Brane Couplings

**Independent research · single author**

**Overview**

This project asks whether restoring the metric to characteristic gauge-theoretic couplings through the Hodge star can produce genuinely new local D-brane interactions. The paper derives a precise representative-dependence criterion and, at leading order for the D4-brane, proves a no-go result: every Hodge-completed coupling lies within a known sector.

<details>
<summary><strong>Motivation</strong></summary>

A cohomology class captures global information, while a Hodge square depends on the particular differential-form representative. This difference provides a natural place to search for local couplings beyond topological data. The project tests that possibility directly and identifies the obstruction, together with where extrinsic brane geometry could first change the conclusion.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Topics studied</strong></summary>

- Hodge theory, differential forms, codifferentials, and harmonic representatives
- Variational bicomplexes and local BRST cohomology
- Differential cohomology and gerbes
- Characteristic classes, transgression, and Chern–Simons/Wess–Zumino descent
- D-brane effective actions, DBI, Wess–Zumino couplings, and $\kappa$-symmetry
- T-duality constraints and anomaly inflow

</details>

## Research Notes

### Iterated Conformal Infinity Is Not Iterated Holography

*Depth-Two Conformal Infinity, Cornered Geometry, and the Limits of Recursive Holography*

A short research note rather than a full project, asking whether holography can be iterated by allowing a boundary to become a new bulk. It shows that conformal infinity determines only a conformal class, so a second asymptotic geometry requires additional structure. The $\mathrm{AdS}_d\subset\mathrm{AdS}_{d+1}$ example suggests a relative or defect interpretation, without claiming a complete second holographic dictionary.
